Summary of Cookie Auth - POST /api/snwebrtc/webrtccookieauth/cookieauth

This API endpoint provides a short-lived WebSocket ticket that the WebRTC phone widget uses to connect to the voice service and initiate calls. It allows guest users to place calls without requiring login, facilitating easy and secure voice communication integration within ServiceNow environments.

Show full answer Show less

Key Features

  • Unauthenticated Access: The endpoint does not require user login, enabling guest call capabilities.
  • Trusted Orchestrator Domains: Tickets are only issued if the orchestratorhost matches or is a subdomain of domains listed in the snwebrtc.orchestrator.trusteddomains system property. If this property is empty, the default trusted domain is sncapps.service-now.com. Only users with the maint role can modify this property.
  • Request Requirements: The request must be a POST with content type application/json and include the session CSRF token in the X-UserToken header.
  • Request Body Parameters:
    • voiceserviceid (required): The 32-character lowercase hexadecimal sysid of the voice service configuration.
    • orchestratorhost (required): The hostname or HTTPS URL of the voice orchestrator, strictly no HTTP, ports, paths, queries, or credentials allowed, and must be trusted.
    • instancename (required): The ServiceNow instance identifier, supporting lowercase alphanumeric and hyphens, max 63 characters.

Status Codes and Responses

  • 200: Request successful; returns a wsticket that is single-use and expires after 60 seconds for WebSocket connection.
  • 400: Bad request due to invalid parameters, wrong content type, oversized body, or untrusted orchestrator host. Response body returns {"error": "Bad Request"}.
  • 502: Bad Gateway when the ServiceNow instance cannot obtain a ticket from the voice orchestrator. Response returns {"error": "Bad Gateway"}.

Practical Use for ServiceNow Customers

ServiceNow customers can leverage this API to securely enable WebRTC voice calling in their applications, even for guest users, by obtaining a short-lived ticket that authenticates the WebRTC phone widget with the voice orchestrator. This mechanism ensures calls are securely routed through trusted orchestrators configured in your instance. Correctly setting trusted domains and passing the required parameters and headers are essential for successful integration.

Example Request

The typical POST request includes the instance URL, request headers with CSRF token, and JSON body with voiceserviceid and orchestratorhost. The response returns a single-use wsticket for establishing the WebSocket connection.

URL format

Default URL: /api/sn_webrtc/webrtc_cookie_auth/cookie_auth

Trusted orchestrator domains

The Cookie Auth POST endpoint creates a ticket only when the orchestrator_host value matches a domain in the following system property, or is a subdomain of one of those domains. If the property is empty, the endpoint uses the default domain, sncapps.service-now.com.

Trusted domains system property
Property Description Default value
sn_webrtc.orchestrator.trusted_domains Comma-separated list of trusted domains. A host is trusted when it equals one of the domains or is a subdomain of one of them. Only users with the maint role can change this property.

Data type: String

cURL request

The following example demonstrates how to use the POST endpoint to request a ticket for a voice service. The request includes the session CSRF token header.

curl "https://instance.service-now.com/api/sn_webrtc/webrtc_cookie_auth/cookie_auth" \
        --request POST \
        --header "Accept: application/json" \
        --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
        --header "X-UserToken: session_csrf_token" \
        --data "{\"voice_service_id\": \"0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef\", \"orchestrator_host\": \"https://myservicenoworchestrator.sncapps.service-now.com\"}"

Response body. The response contains the ticket.

{
        "ws_ticket": "ticket_value"
